Matchbook Learning Morning Meeting · K–2 Behavior Toolkit · Asking for a Break07

Slide 1 · Title & Promise R2

Hold up a break card. “Sometimes our body needs a short break. We do not run away or yell. We ask. We can show our break card, or we can use our words.” Say together: “Can I have a break, please?”

Look for

  • Eyes on the slide or on you
  • Students repeat the line
  • Students notice the break card

If it breaks

  • If students shout the line: “Calm voice. That is how we ask.” Say it once more together, quietly.

Support adult

  • Sit beside any student who has had a hard morning

Language support

  • Hold up the card as you say “break card”
  • Spanish: descanso, tarjeta · Kreyòl: poz, kat

Engagement move Equity stick: pull one name. “Show me how you hold up a break card.” Holding up a hand is a full answer.

A break is a tool, not a reward and not a punishment. Students who can ask for a break do not need to escape the room to get one.

Slide 2 · Regulate · Get Calm First R1

Model the gesture with them every time. “Smell the flower. Blow out the candle. Long and slow. Three times.” Do it with the class, not from the front.

Look for

  • Exhale longer than inhale
  • Shoulders drop
  • Gesture copied

If it breaks

  • If silliness: model silently once, then invite them back.

Support adult

  • Breathe audibly beside any student who cannot settle

Language support

  • No language demand; gesture carries it
  • Same two gestures used in every K–2 lesson

Engagement move LiveSchool: award a point to a student who breathes all three times with you. Name the behavior: “You breathed slow three times.”

Tell the class: “Breathing is one tool. Today we learn another one: asking for a break.”

Slide 3 · Orient · The Story R2, R3

Point to each picture as you tell it. “It was center time, and the room got loud. Lee’s body felt like too much. She did not run away. She did not yell. She held up her break card. Her teacher said, ‘Yes. Take your break.’ Lee sat in the calm corner and turned over the sand timer. She took slow belly breaths. When the sand was done, she came back to her center and tried again. Her teacher said, ‘Welcome back. You asked the calm way.’” Then have the class say together: “Card or words. Wait for a yes. Take a break. Come back.”

Look for

  • Students follow the pictures in order
  • Whole class repeats the We say line

If it breaks

  • If students say Lee is in trouble: “No. Lee asked for a break. That is a smart choice.”

Support adult

  • Point to each panel as the teacher narrates

Language support

  • Four pictures, one or two words each; numbers carry the order
  • Show “too much” by covering your ears, then lowering your hands slowly

Engagement move Equity stick: “Which picture shows Lee asking? Point.” Pointing is a full answer.

The last step matters most. A break ends, and the student comes back. Name the coming back every time you see it.

Slide 4 · Connect · Turn and Talk R3, R4

Show knee to knee with a student partner. “Turn knee to knee. Look at Lee. The room feels like too much. Tell your partner: Lee can ___.” Give 30 seconds, then ring back. Ask one pair: “What did your partner say?”

Look for

  • Partners face each other
  • Students name asking for a break or point to a picture
  • Some students name another calm tool

If it breaks

  • If a pair is stuck: kneel in and say the stem with them.
  • If partners argue: “Take turns. You go first, then you.”

Support adult

  • Pair any student who needs support with a steady partner before the lesson starts

Language support

  • Pointing to a picture is a complete answer
  • Spanish: “Lee puede pedir un descanso” · Kreyòl: “Lee ka mande yon poz”

Engagement move Equity stick: call two names to share. Every calm tool on the slide is a right answer.

All three pictures are good choices. Asking for a break is the one we practice today.

Slide 5 · Practice · Watch Me, Then Show Me R3, R4, R5

Invite one student to the front to model with you. You play the teacher. “Show me your card, or ask me with words.” The student holds up the card or says, “Can I have a break, please?” Answer: “Yes. Take your break.” The student walks to the calm corner, turns the timer, takes one breath, and walks back. Say: “Welcome back.” Then the whole class practices the words together in a calm voice, and everyone holds up a hand as a pretend card.

Look for

  • Calm voice or a raised card
  • The student waits for your yes before moving
  • The student walks back on their own

If it breaks

  • Excellent model: “Show us again. Everyone, watch how she waits for my yes.”
  • Partly right model: “You asked in a calm voice. Now wait for my yes before you go. Try again.”
  • Silly model: “Thank you. Let’s see it the calm way.” Call a new student; no commentary.

Support adult

  • Practice the words first with any student who rarely speaks in a group, then let them use the card instead.

Language support

  • The card is a full answer; no words are needed
  • Spanish: “¿Puedo tomar un descanso, por favor?” · Kreyòl: “Èske m ka pran yon poz, souple?”

Engagement move LiveSchool: award the student model a point. Name it out loud: “You asked the calm way, and you came back.”

Sometimes the answer is “Not yet.” Practice it once: “Not yet. Belly breathe at your seat, and I will come to you.” Waiting calmly is part of the skill.

Slide 6 · Commit · My Promise Today R2, R5

Put your hand on your heart. “Say it with me: I can ask for a break with my words or my card.” Then: “When it feels like too much, what can you do? Point to one.” Model it first: “I can ask for a break.”

Look for

  • Every student says the promise
  • Every student points to one picture

If it breaks

  • If a student does not choose: offer two pictures and let them point.

Support adult

  • Show the break card again to any student who points to the calm corner: “Ask first, then go.”

Language support

  • Hand on heart carries the promise
  • Spanish: Puedo pedir un descanso · Kreyòl: Mwen ka mande yon poz

Engagement move Equity stick: pull three names: “Which one did you point to?” Pointing counts.

Slide 7 · Transition · How We Leave R1, R4, R5

“How we leave is how we start our learning. Now: stand up. Calm body. Walk. Ready to learn.” Do not time this at K–2.

Look for

  • Calm bodies while moving
  • Calm walking, not rushing

If it breaks

  • “Let’s try that again. Back to your spot.” Rebuild clean, no commentary on individuals.

Support adult

  • Stand at the destination, not behind the group

Language support

  • Four icons, four words
  • No timing pressure at this age

Engagement move LiveSchool: award a point to the table that walks with calm bodies the whole way.

Put a break card where every student can reach one this week. When a student asks the calm way, say yes whenever you can.
